label: GO late in episode, after a rewarded common trial, committing strongly to a2
explanation: Fires only at GO (never D1/D2), only when the D1 reward input was 1 (prev_reward==1, 98% of mass), and almost only when the policy strongly favors a2 (choice logit < -6; 99% of mass on model_act==2), and only late in the episode (ep_trial >= ~65; value-head output < 7.13, which marks late trials). Silent after rare transitions (prev_common==0), i.e. after rare-rewarded trials where a model-based agent should switch, and silent after unrewarded trials. Effectively a late-episode, rewarded-and-staying-on-a2 detector. Magnitude ramps up over consecutive rewarded a2 GO steps; low-quartile activations include weak a1 GO steps and early-in-run trials, which the predicate misses (but these hold only ~3% of mass). False positives are mostly the first GO in a run of a2 stays, before the ramp builds. Uses only observed variables and the agent own policy/value; an ep_trial >= 72 variant scores similarly (dev F1 0.87).

issues: All the core claims check out (dev). The unit is active only at GO: D1 and D2 have 0 active steps each. After prev_reward == 0 it carries only 1.8% of the mass. After a rare previous transition (prev_common == 0) it is essentially silent: 0.3% of mass, and adding prev_common == 0 to the predicate gives precision 0.026. model_act == 2 holds 98.7% of the mass. It is never active before ep_trial 60, and only 0.1% of the mass falls in trials 60-69, so in practice it starts around trial 70 rather than 65. The value cut and ep_trial >= 72 score the same.
The test scores reproduce: P 0.889, R 0.856, F1 0.872, mass recall 0.967.

Small imprecision in the label: 'after a rewarded common trial' always means the previous trial was a2 to S2 (common), rewarded. Restricting to prev_action == 1 leaves 2 predicted steps and 0 hits. All of the mass is either prev_action == 2 (75%) or the window's first trial, where the previous action is unknown (22%). The cleaner reading is 'previous trial was a2, common transition, rewarded, and the agent stays on a2 late in the episode'. choice < -6 mostly stands in for the unknown previous action at rel -3.

The claim that magnitude 'builds up over consecutive rewarded a2 GO steps' is only partly supported. When the trial before the last was also rewarded, precision rises to 0.94, versus 0.79 when it was unrewarded, which fits the explanation's account of false positives. But one top window reaches the maximum activation (1.00) on the first rewarded GO right after an r0 trial. So the build-up is a tendency, not a rule.

Misses on dev and test hold 3.3% of the mass and are scattered weak activations: a1 GO steps with activation around 0.01-0.2, and a few GO steps after r0. False positives fall where the stated factors are borderline (earlier in the episode, weaker choice logit, an unrewarded trial two back), with subset precision of 0.6-0.8 in each case. These are graded edges, not a separate silent class.

Refinements did not beat the original by more than 0.003 dev F1: tightening to choice < -7, adding ep_trial >= 70, changing the value cut, or gating on the reward two trials back. No better predicate was found.
